To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ompK36 genotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of K. pneumoniae strains may predict their responses to antimicrobial treatment regimens.

the activity of gentamicin against gentamicin-suitable K. pneumoniae strains was superior to that of doripenen and colistin, alone and in combinations, and that the ompK36 genotype was associated with the activity of doripenam, gentamicin, and colistin.
gentamicin, doripenem, and colistin, alone and in combinations, are active against K. pneumoniae strains that produce the KPC-2 carbapenemase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and efficient antimicrobial agents for treating multidrug-resistant bacteria.

the development of an algorithm for predicting the activity of various antimicrobial combinations, alone and in combination, against gentamicin-suscceptible, K. pneumoniae strains that produce the carbapenemases Klebsiella Pneumoniae Carbapenemase-2 (KPC-2) and Klebsiella Protease Carbapenemases-2 (Klebsiella Proteases-2) and that have various ompK36 genotypic profiles.
the development of new and improved methods for the treatment of bacterial infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

doripenem and colistin, alone and in combinations, were not inferior to gentamicin, alone or in combinations, against KPC-producing strains with various genotypes of OmpK36 porin, and that gentamicin doses of at least 8 μg/ml are needed to achieve a bactericidal effect against these strains.
the use of gentamicin and colistin alone and in combinations, as well as the use of the 3-drug doripenem-colisitin-gentamicin regimen, is not supported by the data presented here.

the combination of colistin (1 μg/ml) with doripenem and/or gentamicin (both at 2 μg/ml each) would be the most effective treatment for KPC-2producing K. pneumoniae isolates with glycine/aspartic acid insert at aa positions 134 and/or 135.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the ompK36 genotype can influence the activity of gentamicin, doripenem, and colistin against KPC-producing Klebsielle pneumoniae strains.

we have shown that the combination of dorpienem-colistine was superior to the combination gentamicin-colistine against strains with glycyl-aspartyl insertion in ompK36 at aa positions 134 and aa135, and that the combination of gentamicin-colisitne was superior against strains with glycil-asparagyl insertion at the same positions.
the combination of gentamicin and colistin was superior to the other 2- and 3-drug combinations against strains with glycines and aspartic acids at aa positions 134 and/or 135 of OmpK36.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gentamicin and colistin, alone and in combinations, can be used to treat KPC-producing Klebsiellapneumoniae strains that are susceptible to these agents.
we can use the genotypes of the OmpK36 porins to predict the efficacy of different antimicrobial agents.
the presence of glycine or aspartic acid in OpmK35 porin at positions 134 and/or 135 is associated with resistance to gentamicin, doripenem, colistin, and their combinations.
